title: A-trade grading followups -- non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #180 (backend-trade-grading-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: `backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_closed_trades.py::TestGetClosedTradesSharesOneFetchPerTicker::test_two_trades_same_ticker_only_filter_and_channel_once`'s docstring, and the corresponding decision entry in `docs/tasks/done/backend-trade-grading-followups.json` (rationale field), describe the regression this test guards against as 'not the pre-fix once-per-row' -- wording that implies the monkeypatched `dropna_calls`/`autoenvelope_calls` counters would read 2 (once per closed-trade row) if the O(n)-per-row bug were reintroduced by reverting `_grade_closed_trades` to call `grade_closed_trade` per row. Experimentally verified (by temporarily reverting `_grade_closed_trades` to the pre-fix per-row `grade_closed_trade` call and re-running just this test) that the counters actually read 0, not 2: `drop_malformed_daily_bars`/`autoenvelope` are separate module-level name bindings in `app.portfolio.grading` versus `app.api.routers.portfolio`, and the test's `monkeypatch.setattr(portfolio_router, ...)` only intercepts the router module's own binding -- the pre-fix code path never called through that binding at all, so reverting drops the count to 0 rather than raising it to 2. The test still correctly fails on that regression (`assert 0 == 1` vs. the intended `assert 2 == 1`), so this is not a functional test gap -- just an inaccurate description of the exact failure mode in the test's own docstring and the decision rationale that could confuse a future reader debugging why the assertion output doesn't match what's described. Fix: reword the test docstring (and optionally the decision entry, though decisions are historical record and don't strictly need editing) to say the counters would read 0 (never invoked through the router's own binding) rather than implying a doubled count.

decisions.decision: Reworded only the test's own docstring in backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_closed_trades.py to state the counters would read 0 (never invoked through the router's own drop_malformed_daily_bars/autoenvelope bindings on a revert), not 2. Left docs/tasks/done/backend-trade-grading-followups.json's historical decision-entry rationale untouched.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item itself flags the decision-entry edit as optional ('decisions are historical record and don't strictly need editing'), and that task is already done/merged -- editing a done task's own decisions array to retroactively correct wording would blur the distinction between 'what was believed true at the time' and 'what's true now', which is exactly what the historical-record framing in CLAUDE.md's decision-memory section is for. The test docstring is the one place a future reader would actually consult while debugging a real assertion failure, so that's where the fix needs to land; this task's own file (visible from docs/tasks/index.json) is the durable record of the correction for anyone who does want the fuller context. Implemented as part of a batched PR alongside backend-indicator-atr-adx-followups, backend-divergence-detection-followups, and backend-kangaroo-tail-pattern-followups (four small non-blocking-followups tasks on one branch/PR per explicit user request).
